findings.claim: The FEC issued a formal warning letter dated April 28, 2026 to Clement's Senate committee (STATE OF LOC NATION FOR CLEMENT FOR SENATE, ID C00857128) after she reported a $50.25 million self-loan in her Q1 2026 filing, and the FEC subsequently moved the loan entry out of its searchable database into its 'False and Fictitious Filings' miscellaneous repository on the committee's page. The amount is 10x larger than any other self-loan in the 2026 election cycle.
findings.evidence: OpenSecrets (Joedy McCreary, May 15, 2026): 'A write‑in Senate candidate in Georgia who reported loaning her own campaign more than $50 million has drawn a warning letter from the Federal Election Commission saying the filing may be inaccurate and reminding her that knowingly submitting false information can carry civil or criminal penalties. ... The FEC on Friday then removed the loan entry from its searchable online database and placed it in a separate repository for miscellaneous documents on the committee's page, agency spokesperson Myles Martin said. ... [FEC] filings deemed unverified or potentially false are moved to the commission's “False and Fictitious Filings” section, where they remain public but are excluded from its searchable database and campaign finance statistics.' The FEC committee page itself (C00857128) shows three 'Miscellaneous Report to FEC 2026' entries (FEC-1972827, dated 05/05/2026, 7 pages; plus filings dated 04/12/2026 and 02/10/2026) under 'Other documents' — consistent with FEC's documented process of moving questionable filings out of mainline reports.

sources.access_notes: Referenced from OpenSecrets article as the April 28, 2026 FEC warning letter; not directly scraped but content described verbatim by OpenSecrets which is the primary reporting outlet for FEC RAD review documents.

findings.confidence_rationale: Two independent primary sources (FEC.gov committee page + OpenSecrets investigative piece) plus FEC spokesperson on the record. The FEC committee page itself shows the miscellaneous-filing reclassification.

findings.claim: Clement's $50.25M reported self-loan is not cash; it is the asserted fair-market value of a license to her own 'Loc Nation Dollar' (LND) intellectual property — a sovereign-currency framework she calls 'the official Black dollar' pegged at '1 LND = $750 USD' by her own published policy. findings.evidence: OpenSecrets: 'Clement said the filing reflects a complex valuation of a license to her own currency-related intellectual property and referred OpenSecrets to a website describing the “LND” monetary unit, but did not provide evidence that any funds were deposited into the campaign's account.' And: 'Clement's response to OpenSecrets included a set of self‑prepared notarized documents asserting that the campaign's reported $50.25 million “loan” reflects the value of a limited non‑exclusive license to her own intellectual property... But they do not include any evidence showing that $50 million was ever deposited into the campaign's account. Nor do they demonstrate the existence of liquid funds corresponding to the amount reported to the FEC.' John Martin, election-law professor at Quinnipiac, told OpenSecrets the filing is plausibly 'a typo, or it's fabricated... I wouldn't be surprised if somebody forged a self-loan to profit off third-party contributions.'
findings.confidence_rationale: OpenSecrets obtained the campaign's own response to the FEC and quotes Clement directly; primary source (her own website) confirms the LND framework and the 1 LND = $750 USD peg.

findings.claim: On the available evidence as of May 22, 2026, there is NO documented operational connection between Christina Loren Clement / State of LOC Nation and Rico Cortez Dukes / THEYFEARTRUTH FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF AMERICA. The two operators share a pattern (self-declared sovereign government, 2024 FEC presidential candidacy, LDA filing under their own self-government entity, prolific self-publishing) but no shared address, registered agent, lawyer, court filing, corporate officer, or social-media cross-pollination has surfaced. Searches for 'Rico Dukes' + 'Christina Clement' / 'LOC Nation' return only flat directory listings (Politics1's 2028 presidential candidates registry lists both as separate, unaffiliated entries). Their digital footprints are disjoint: Clement at @dynastyhealing / queenclc1 (Atlanta-Dover-Apopka triangle), Dukes at @official_son_of_huey_p_newton (Shreveport-Dallas).
findings.evidence: Three targeted searches ('\"Rico Dukes\" \"Christina Clement\"', '\"Rico Dukes\" Christina OR Clement OR \"loc nation\" connection collaboration', '\"State of LOC Nation\" OR \"LOC Nation\" reparations sovereign') returned zero co-mentions. Politics1's 2028 presidential candidates page lists 'Christina Clement (DE)' (at line 429) and 'Rico Dukes (I-TX)' (at line 716) as separate alphabetical entries with no cross-reference. Geography is disjoint: Dukes founded THEYFEARTRUTH at '1818 Coriscana St in Dallas' per his Wikimedia self-bio; Clement operates from Atlanta GA, Apopka FL (2787 S Orange Blossom Trl per Northrop Grumman bankruptcy creditor matrix), and Dover DE (Christina Loren Clement LLC).
findings.confidence_rationale: Negative finding. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence — a private connection (shared lawyer, off-line meeting) cannot be ruled out from open-source signal. But the affirmative null across multiple OSINT vectors supports 'independent sovereign-citizen-style filers occupying the same niche, not a coordinated network' over 'operationally connected'. The Spotlight finding stands as: distinct cells of a broader movement, not a single network.
